Perform a permutation correlation test on every row of a matrix

Source: R/permutation.R
permutation_correlation_test.Rd

Compute a correlation value for every row of X against the vector y and n_perm random permutations of y. If the number of distinct permutations of y is less than or equal to n_perm then an exact test using all permutations is performed instead. In both cases the function returns a data.frame of the original data with additional columns for the test statistic, permutation p-value, and FDR corrected p-value.

Usage

permutation_correlation_test(
  X,
  y,
  n_perm = 10000,
  method = c("pearson", "spearman"),
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  chunk_size = 1000,
  n_core = 1
)

Arguments

X

numeric matrix or data.frame that can be converted to a numeric matrix

y

numeric vector of values to correlate with rows of X

n_perm

integer. The desired number of permutations to sample from. Default (10,000)

method

character. One of "pearson" (default) or "spearman"

alternative

character. One of "two.sided" (default), "greater" or "less"

chunk_size

integer. Number of permutations to process at once. Controls memory usage, nrow(X) x chunk_size correlations are held in memory at a time. Default (1000)

n_core

integer. The number of cores to use for processing chunks of permutations. Default (1)

Value

data.frame containing the original values in X along with columns 'cor', 'empirical.p', and 'FDR'

Details

Exact p-values are computed as the proportion of all distinct permutations (including the observed ordering) with a correlation at least as extreme as the observed value. When permutations are randomly sampled, p-values are computed with statmod::permp() (if installed), which gives exact p-values for permutations sampled with replacement (Phipson & Smyth 2010). Otherwise the conservative estimate (b + 1) / (n_perm + 1) is used.

Correlations are computed by standardizing the rows of X once and performing matrix multiplication against chunks of permuted y. Rows of X containing missing values or with zero variance return NA.

References

Phipson B, Smyth GK (2010). Permutation P-values should never be zero: calculating exact P-values when permutations are randomly drawn. Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology 9, Article 39.

Examples

# generate example data
X <- matrix(runif(1e3 * 10), nrow = 1e3, ncol = 10)
y <- 1:10
dimnames(X) <- list(paste("feature", 1:1e3, sep = "."), paste("sample", 1:10, sep = "."))

# correlate each row of X with 1,000 random permutations of vector y
res <- permutation_correlation_test(X, y, n_perm = 1e3, method = "spearman")
